chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from Ibn Ribat, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

From the urethra there comes out mani, madhy, wady, and wadhy. As for mani, it is that by which the bones become relaxed and the body becomes fatigued, and it requires ghusl. As for madhy, it comes out from desire and there is nothing due because of it. As for wady, it is what comes out after urination. As for wadhy, it is what comes out from ailments, and there is nothing due because of it.

As for the report narrated by al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: 'Three come out from the urethra, and they are mani, from which ghusl is due; and wady, from which wudu is due because it comes out from the channel of urine.' He said: 'And as for madhy, there is no wudu in it; it is only like what comes out from the nose.' His statement, 'and wady, from which wudu is due,' is understood to mean that if one had not performed istibra' after urination in the manner that we shall mention later, and wady came out from him, then wudu becomes obligatory for him, because it does not come out except with some urine accompanying it. Do you not see his statement, 'because it comes out from the channel of urine,' indicating that urine is with it? Were it not so, repeating wudu because of it would not be obligatory.

What clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning a man who urinates, then cleans himself, then afterward finds moisture. He said: 'When he urinates, then he should stroke what is between the anus and the testicles three times, and press what is between them, then clean himself; then if something flows until it reaches the ساق, he should not be concerned with it.'

key_terms.الْإِحْلِيلِ: the urethral passage from which these fluids emerge
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, whose trace may accompany wady and affect the ruling
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required upon emission of mani
key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: pre-seminal fluid emerging from desire, with no wudu or ghusl due because of it
key_terms.الْمَنِيُّ: semen; the fluid whose emission requires ghusl
key_terms.الْوَدْيُ: a fluid that comes out after urination; discussed in relation to wudu when mixed with urine
key_terms.الْوَذْيُ: a discharge associated with ailment, with no ritual consequence by itself
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), discussed here regarding discharge linked to urine

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on mani, madhy, wady, and other fluids in relation to wudu and ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the different fluids that may exit from the male organ and explains their legal consequences for taharah. It distinguishes mani, which requires ghusl, from other fluids such as madhy, wady, and wadhy, while also clarifying the role of istibra' after urination in determining whether wudu is required.
